translations.answer: The response has not confirmed. The responder points out that friction, mass, debris, and ground softness may still disrupt migration; and that the scan cadence needs to be designed for continuous field changes. Therefore, scan fidelity cannot replace physical parameter validation and runtime change detection.
translations.applicability: Applicable to field reconstruction schemes that claim to require no real-time micro-tuning.
translations.credibility.rationale: The solution has not closed or there is conflicting information; only a problem is formed at this point.
translations.details.attempts.0: Generate a Gaussian Splat and collision mesh using a 360° scan, and train an RGB strategy in the same scene.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Verify that the visual reconstruction and collision mesh come from the same field and scale; record friction, mass, ground softness, and field changes.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: The original post's candidate solution was field reconstruction plus a same-source collision mesh, combined with domain randomization and a large visual encoder.
translations.details.environments.0: Real-world office 360° scan; Gaussian Splat scale; same-source collision mesh; Isaac Sim/Lab; RGB-only navigation strategy.
translations.details.limits.0: No information on the robot, task success rate, randomization parameters, failure cases, or independent reproducibility; the response points out that debris, ground softness, and re-scan cadence are still boundaries.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The author claims that no real-time micro-tuning is needed for deployment, and that field adaptation can be done in days instead of months; the original post does not include quantitative validation.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: An RGB strategy in general-purpose random geometry and no-texture simulation is difficult to generalize to real-world deployment settings.
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before deploying on real-world fields, validate the collision mesh, depth occlusion, glass doors, and ground compliance in low-speed, limited-force, and collision-avoidance conditions.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Inconsistent visual appearance and physical collision geometry; domain randomization does not cover debris, friction, mass, or ground softness; field changes make the previous scan outdated.
translations.details.symptoms.0: General dummy scenarios teach structure only, and cannot cover real materials, lighting, or semantics; real-time collision with a real robot could cause hardware damage and long reinitializations.
translations.media_summaries.0: The visible screenshot shows the first half of the original post, confirming that it compares a general-purpose random, no-texture scenario with a real-world office reconstruction; the screenshot lacks logs, physical parameters, or success rate curves, so it cannot validate the 'zero real-time micro-tuning' conclusion.
translations.source.title: Training an RGB humanoid robot strategy in real-world deployment settings
translations.title: Can field scanning alone ensure zero real-time micro-tuning in sim-to-real?
